repos.fit: 候选人擅长 AI Infra，但目前没有高性能 GPU。挑选的任务集中在调度器状态机、权重加载逻辑、API 协议层（OpenAI/Anthropic 兼容性）以及 Tokenizer 编码逻辑。这些任务完全可以在 CPU 环境下通过单元测试或离线推理引擎状态机进行验证，且对 SGLang 的生产环境稳定性至关重要。
repos.current_direction: SGLang 目前在快速迭代支持最新的前沿模型（如 DeepSeek-V4.1, Qwen3 等），同时在完善其生产级 Serving 能力（如 API 兼容性、计费指标、多语言前端对齐）。
recommended_order: [Bug] DeepSeek-V4.1 encoder renders the pre-release reasoning-effort budgets (high → 50; release reference and deepseek-recipe → 75)
[Bug] /v1/messages never reports cache_creation_input_tokens, so cache writes are billed as plain input
[Bug] /v1/messages streaming thinking blocks can end without a signature
[Bug] OpenAI Chat Completions: Python SSE chunks have inconsistent id and created
[Bug] FP8 KV cache scales are silently dropped when loading Qwen3-MoE / Qwen2 / Mixtral and every layer falls back to scale 1.0
Retracted input_embeds requests silently splice two generations into one successful response (send_token_offset survives the discard of output_ids)
maintainer_path: 1. 从 API 协议层和模型特定的编码逻辑入手，熟悉 SGLang 的前端请求处理链路。
2. 深入权重加载与量化参数映射，理解 SGLang 如何在底层对接不同架构的模型。
3. 攻克调度器状态机中的复杂 Bug，掌握核心的请求生命周期管理，最终能够独立负责核心调度逻辑的重构与优化。

tasks.goal: 在 Anthropic 兼容的 `/v1/messages` 接口中，正确报告 `cache_creation_input_tokens`。
tasks.first_action: 调查 `python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/anthropic/` 下的 usage 映射逻辑，提取底层引擎返回的 cache write 指标。

确保非流式路径也应用相同的 fallback 逻辑。

tasks.title: [Bug] OpenAI Chat Completions: Python SSE chunks have inconsistent id and created
tasks.source_title: [Bug] OpenAI Chat Completions: Python SSE chunks have inconsistent id and created
tasks.why_core: SSE 流式协议的严格一致性是下游网关和客户端正常工作的基础。解决此问题能建立对异步流式处理和请求上下文管理的深刻理解。
tasks.goal: 确保同一个 Chat Completion 请求产生的所有 SSE chunk 具有相同的 `id` 和 `created` 时间戳。
tasks.first_action: 在请求初始化时生成并固定 `id` 和 `created`，并在所有 chunk 中复用。
implementation_steps: 定位 OpenAI 兼容 API 的流式处理逻辑（可能在 `python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/`）。
检查 `id` 和 `created` 的生成位置。目前可能是在每个 chunk 生成时动态创建的。
将 `id` 和 `created` 的生成提前到请求级别，并保存在请求上下文中。
在生成每个 SSE chunk 时，从请求上下文中读取这两个字段。
编写测试，使用 `n > 1` 发起流式请求，断言所有 chunk 的 `id` 和 `created` 完全一致。
validation: 发起 `n=2` 的流式请求，捕获所有 SSE chunk，断言它们的 `id` 和 `created` 字段完全相同。
questions: Rust 前端目前表现正常，是否需要参考 Rust 前端的实现逻辑来重构 Python 前端的上下文管理？
risks: 如果在多候选生成（n>1）时底层引擎是独立返回结果的，可能需要在前端进行额外的状态聚合。

tasks.source_title: [Bug] FP8 KV cache scales are silently dropped when loading Qwen3-MoE / Qwen2 / Mixtral and every layer falls back to scale 1.0
tasks.why_core: 权重加载和量化参数映射是推理引擎的基石。修复此问题能避免严重的静默精度损失，是深入模型架构和量化机制的绝佳机会。
tasks.goal: 修复 Qwen3-MoE、Qwen2 和 Mixtral 模型加载 FP8 KV cache scales 时因名称映射错误导致 scale 丢失的问题。
tasks.first_action: 在相关模型文件中引入并使用 `maybe_remap_kv_scale_name` 函数。
implementation_steps: 定位 `python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_moe.py`, `qwen2.py`, `mixtral.py`。
引入 `python/sglang/srt/model_loader/weight_utils.py` 中的 `maybe_remap_kv_scale_name`。
在 `stacked_params_mapping` 循环处理权重名称时，对 scale 相关的 tensor 名称应用该重映射函数，避免被错误的子串替换逻辑破坏。
编写离线测试，加载带有 FP8 KV scale 的 dummy checkpoint，断言加载后的 `k_scale` 和 `v_scale` 不为 1.0。
validation: 在 CPU 环境下加载一个包含 FP8 KV scale 的小型 Qwen2 模型，打印 `model.layers[0].self_attn.attn.k_scale`，确认其值等于 checkpoint 中的真实值而非 1.0。
questions: 除了这三个模型，是否还有其他使用手写 weight loader 的模型存在类似的子串替换风险？

tasks.title: Retracted input_embeds requests silently splice two generations into one successful response (send_token_offset survives the discard of output_ids)
tasks.source_title: Retracted input_embeds requests silently splice two generations into one successful response (send_token_offset survives the discard of output_ids)
tasks.why_core: 调度器的状态机管理是推理引擎最核心、最复杂的部分。解决请求重试导致的状态泄漏问题，能证明你具备维护核心调度逻辑的能力。
tasks.goal: 在请求因 OOM 被 retract 时，彻底重置所有输出流相关的 offset 状态，防止新旧生成结果拼接。
tasks.first_action: 在 `Req.reset_for_retract()` 中添加对 `send_token_offset` 及相关游标的重置逻辑。
implementation_steps: 定位 `python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py` 中的 `reset_for_retract` 方法。
在 `self.input_embeds is not None` 分支中，除了清空 `output_ids`，还需将 `send_token_offset`、`send_decode_id_offset` 等输出流游标重置为 0。
检查 `init_incremental_detokenize` 相关的增量 detokenizer 游标（如 `surr_offset`, `read_offset`），确保它们在 retract 时也被正确重置。
编写纯 Python 的状态机单元测试，模拟请求生成一半被 retract 然后重新生成的过程，断言最终输出的 token 序列完整且无截断。
validation: 执行 Issue 中描述的状态机复现步骤（无需 GPU），断言 `reset_for_retract()` 执行后，`send_token_offset` 为 0，且后续的 `output_ids_` 切片逻辑能正确获取完整的重新生成序列。
questions: 除了 `send_token_offset` 和 `send_decode_id_offset`，是否还有其他在 request 级别维护的流式状态需要在 retract 时重置？
risks: 重置游标可能导致客户端收到重复的 token（如果客户端不具备处理重试的能力），需确认 SGLang 的流式协议对 retract 的预期行为。

issues.title: Rust TreeCore (v0.5.19) shows e2e regression at concurrency on small dense model
issues.body:
> **Follow-up (2026-09-17):** The original approximately 11–12% E2E slowdown was not reproduced across six independent Python/Rust session pairs under a revised warmed protocol. The CPU-saving/blocking interpretation below is withdrawn. See the [follow-up results, methodology and limitations](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/38536#issuecomment-5716482108). The original report is retained below for context.

## Summary

The Rust TreeCore backend (`SGLANG_UNIFIED_RADIX_TREE_CORE_BACKEND=rust`), shipped as opt-in in v0.5.19, shows a measurable end-to-end regression at concurrency compared to the Python TreeCore backend, on a small dense model with a short shared prefix workload. The PR (#32710) notes end-to-end benchmarking as a "planned follow-up" — this is an independent data point for that.

## Setup

- **Model**: Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct (dense, bf16)
- **GPU**: RTX 4090 (single GPU, TP=1)
- **Engine**: SGLang v0.5.19 (`lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.19` Docker image)
- **Workload**: streaming tool-call completions with the stock `qwen` tool parser, 2 tool calls per request, 10.2–10.4 deltas/request (identical across all arms — no granularity confound)
- **Shared prefix**: system prompt + tool JSON schema, order hundreds of tokens (not 61K-token class like the C++ PR's benchmark)
- **Concurrency**: 8, 64, 256 concurrent requests; 3 rounds per level, medians reported

## Three-arm A/B

Three arms, same image, same model, same GPU:

| arm | version | TreeCore backend |
|---|---|---|
| `stock` | v0.5.18 | plain RadixCache (no unified tree) |
| `python` | v0.5.19 | Python TreeCore (unified, default) |
| `rust` | v0.5.19 | Rust TreeCore (`SGLANG_UNIFIED_RADIX_TREE_CORE_BACKEND=rust`) |

Baseline for comparison: `python` arm (same version, isolating only the TreeCore backend).

## Results (median of 3 rounds)

| conc | metric | python (0.5.19) | rust (0.5.19) | delta |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8 | stream_span | 189.6 ms | 189.6 ms | −0.0% |
| 8 | e2e p50 | 278 ms | 275 ms | −0.9% |
| 8 | CPU | 172% | 161% | −6% |
| 64 | stream_span | 367.4 ms | 395.3 ms | **+7.6%** |
| 64 | e2e p50 | 606 ms | 678 ms | **+11.9%** |
| 64 | TTFT p50 | 223.7 ms | 249.9 ms | +11.7% |
| 64 | ITL p50 | 11.0 ms | 12.5 ms | +14.2% |
| 64 | CPU | 172% | 161% | −6% |
| 256 | stream_span | 515.9 ms | 562.6 ms | **+9.1%** |
| 256 | e2e p50 | 1208 ms | 1340 ms | **+10.9%** |
| 256 | TTFT p50 | 664.2 ms | 752.2 ms | +13.2% |
| 256 | ITL p50 | 24.8 ms | 24.3 ms | −1.8% |
| 256 | CPU | 172% | 161% | −6% |

`stream_span` is a delta-count-invariant metric (total streaming wall time / number of deltas), so it is not confounded by arms emitting different chunk counts. Delta counts were identical across all arms at every concurrency level.

IQRs at conc 64: stream_span python IQR 19.8 ms, rust IQR 19.1 ms, against a 28 ms difference. IQRs at conc 256: python IQR 30.2 ms, rust IQR 29.9 ms, against a 47 ms difference. The gap is larger than the spread at both levels.

## Observations

1. **The Rust backend is slower at concurrency, not faster.** At conc 8 the arms are identical. At conc 64 and 256, `stream_span`, e2e, and TTFT all regress by 8–13%.

2. **Rust uses ~6% less CPU while being slower.** This points at blocking/overhead (PyO3 boundary crossings, GIL round-trips, or lock contention) rather than the tree algorithm itself being computationally slow — the CPU savings should have produced a speedup, not a regression.

3. **The engine-version control is clean.** stock (0.5.18, p

issues.title: [Bug] sgl-deep-gemm 0.2.0: SM90 weight-scale transform returns a non-owning alias (follow-up to #32188)
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues and PRs. #32188 fixes the SGLang activation-scale wrapper; this reports a remaining library API path. See also the closed #32097.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest **sgl-deep-gemm PyPI release, 0.2.0**, checked on 2026-09-16. The reproducer does not import SGLang or vLLM.
- [x] Environment information and a minimal reproducer are included.
- [x] This is a bug report written in English.

### Describe the bug

On SM90, `deep_gemm.transform_sf_into_required_layout` can return a tensor aliasing the input scale without retaining the original allocation's owner. Deleting the input allows the PyTorch caching allocator to reuse its storage while the returned tensor is still live. The output then changes to the contents of an unrelated allocation.

Reproduced with the published x86_64 wheels for **sgl-deep-gemm 0.1.7 and 0.2.0**, using PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130 and apache-tvm-ffi 0.1.11 on NVIDIA H20-3e (SM90). Version 0.2.0 was installed into a separate `--target` directory and selected via `PYTHONPATH`; both its distribution version and imported module path were checked. The original shared installation was not modified.

This is a follow-up to **Bug 1 in #32188**, not a new discovery of the general ownership defect. That PR preserves ownership in SGLang's `get_mn_major_tma_aligned_tensor` wrapper and explicitly leaves the library-level fix as follow-up. Here a downstream caller uses `transform_sf_into_required_layout` directly for **weight scales**, so it does not receive that protection. #32097 also identifies this broader API impact.

I am filing here because Issues are disabled on `sgl-project/DeepGEMM`; please redirect this report if another tracking location is preferred.

### Reproduction

Save the following as `repro.py`. Select one idle SM90 GPU. No model, distributed setup, or GEMM execution is required.

```python
"""Run on one idle SM90 GPU; no model or inference framework is required."""
import gc
import importlib.metadata
import json
import sys

import torch
import deep_gemm

print(json.dumps({'sgl-deep-gemm': importlib.metadata.version('sgl-deep-gemm'),
                  'apache-tvm-ffi': importlib.metadata.version('apache-tvm-ffi'),
                  'torch': torch.__version__, 'module_file': deep_gemm.__file__}), flush=True)

clone_output = '--clone' in sys.argv
sf = torch.full((1, 128, 40), 0.0005, device='cuda', dtype=torch.float32)
source_ptr = sf.data_ptr()
out = deep_gemm.transform_sf_into_required_layout(
    sf, 16384, 5120, (1, 128, 128),
    num_groups=1, is_sfa=False, disable_ue8m0_cast=True,
)
if not isinstance(out, torch.Tensor):
    out = torch.from_dlpack(out)
if clone_output:
    out = out.clone()  # Diagnostic control: original owner is still alive here.
torch.cuda.synchronize()
before_nan = out.isnan().sum().item()
aliases_input = out.data_ptr() == source_ptr
del sf
gc.collect()
# Simulate the small allocations made by subsequent model loading/forward work.
buffers = [torch.full((1, 128, 40), float('nan'), device='cuda') for _ in range(20)]
torch.cuda.synchronize()
result = {
    'clone': clone_output,
    'aliases_input': aliases_input,
    'source_pointer_reused': any(x.data_ptr() == source_ptr for x in buffers),
    'before_nan': before_nan,
    'after_nan': out.isnan().sum().item(),
    'numel': out.numel(),
}
print(json.dumps(result), flush=True)

issues.title: [KDA] Fused intra-chunk prefill path (`chunk_kda_fwd_intra(fuse_diagonal=True)`) collapses for strong per-channel decays because of the ±126 clamp in the exp2 factorization
issues.body:
## Summary

`chunk_kda_fwd` selects `chunk_kda_fwd_intra(fuse_diagonal=True, fuse_recompute=True)` whenever
`B * NT * H <= 256` (i.e. for every short prefill). Inside `chunk_kda_fwd_kernel_inter_solve_fused` the
diagonal sub-blocks factorize `exp2(g_i - g_j) = exp2(g_i - g_n) * exp2(g_n - g_j)` and clamp both factors:

```python
b_gm0 = tl.clamp(b_g0 - b_gn0[None, :], -126.0, 126.0)
b_gq0 = tl.where(m_tc0[:, None], exp2(b_gm0), 0.0)
b_gk0 = tl.where(m_tc0[:, None], exp2(-b_gm0), 0.0)
```

When a channel decays by more than 2^126 inside a 16-token sub-block, the clamped factors no longer cancel and the
block's `exp2(g_i - g_j)` is effectively replaced by `exp2(0)`: keys that should have been forgotten are read at full
weight. Kimi Linear's gates are mild enough not to trigger this; models with sharper per-channel decays do
(our model: cumulative log2 decays inside a 64-token chunk down to -485, `exp(A_log)` up to 72).

## Measurements (H200, Triton kernels from main @ 2026-08-03, one real layer's q/k/v/gate/beta, T = 298)

rel-L2 of the chunk output vs an fp32 torch recurrence on identical inputs:

| path | rel-L2 |
|---|---|
| `chunk_kda` heuristic (fused intra, small grid) | 1.52e-1 |
| `chunk_kda` with the token-parallel (unfused) intra path | 2.37e-3 |
| vLLM's fla port `chunk_kda_with_fused_gate` (same inputs) | 2.32e-3 |

End to end (40-layer hybrid model, per-layer comparison against the HF implementation): the first KDA layer is 15 %
off with the fused path and 0.23 % with the unfused one; prompt top-1 agreement 95.3 % vs 97.0 % (the HF fla-vs-torch
reference pair itself agrees 97.3 %).

The effect is gate-magnitude driven: clamping the cumulative gate at -8 (natural log) before the kernel makes fused ==
unfused (2.2e-2 on the pre-#31904 snapshot), i.e. the fused path is exact whenever the ±126 clamp is inactive.

## Proposed mitigation

Per-layer opt-out of the fused path, threaded from the attention layer to the kernel:

- `chunk_kda(..., fused_intra: Optional[bool] = None)` / `chunk_kda_fwd(...)`:
  `_fused_intra = _small_grid if fused_intra is None else bool(fused_intra)`; pass it as `fuse_diagonal` / `fuse_recompute`.
- `TritonKDAKernel.extend(...)` forwards `fused_intra=kwargs.get("fused_intra")`.
- `KDAAttnBackend.forward_extend` passes `fused_intra=getattr(layer, "kda_fused_intra", None)`.
- A model whose gates exceed the clamp sets `self.attn.kda_fused_intra = False` on its `RadixLinearAttention`.

Default behaviour (heuristic) is unchanged for all existing models. A kernel-side alternative would be to detect
`|g_i - g_n| > 126` for the block and fall back to the direct difference form, but that costs every model.

## Related

- #31904 fixed the exponent-base mix (natural-log cumsum vs exp2 intra kernels) in the same file family; snapshots
  before it also show a 2 % floor on the unfused path for such gates (units mismatch, not a precision limit).

# Second (small) issue: `LinearAttnModelSpec.support_mamba_cache_extra_buffer` is ignored

`arg_groups/overrides.py::supports_mamba_cache_extra_buffer` decides from the hardcoded `_MAMBA_EXTRA_BUFFER_ARCHS`
only, so a model registered through `linear_attn_model_registry` with `support_mamba_cache_extra_buffer=True` still
resolves `--mamba-radix-cache-strategy auto` to `no_buffer` (which also forces `disable_overlap_schedule`), and an
explicit `extra_buffer` is rejected by `_validate_mamba_extra_buffer` ("extra_buffer is not supported for
<arch>; use no_buffer"). Proposed fix (

issues.title: # [RFC] Asymmetric P/D deployment for DeepSeek-V4.1 Flash
issues.body:
## Summary This RFC proposes an asymmetric Prefill/Decode deployment for DeepSeek-V4.1 Flash. For a prompt of length `N` and replay window `W = 128`: - The **Prefill worker** processes only the prefix `[0, N-W)` and produces its KV cache. - The **Decode worker** receives that prefix KV and processes the final prompt window `[N-W, N)` as a bounded prefill/replay. - Decode then samples the first output token and continues normal speculative decoding with per-request `q_len = 1 + num_spec_tokens`. The key property is that Decode does not need separate encoder and decoder workloads. Every layer sees the same token count in a given step: ```text first Decode step: L0-L39 process W prompt tokens later Decode steps: L0-L39 process 1 + num_spec_tokens tokens per request ``` ```text P: prompt tokens [0, N-W) -> prefix KV | v D: prompt tokens [N-W, N) -> first output token D: generated tokens -> normal decode / speculative verify ``` The Prefill worker only needs the causal encoder and the decoder's first KV-producing projection path. The Decode worker keeps the full model. The main goal is to remove almost half of the model weights from each Prefill replica. A secondary goal is to avoid running a separate, low-density late-decoder workload on Prefill. Decode remains architecturally simple: its first step is a bounded prefill through the full model, followed by normal decode steps through the same full model. ## Motivation DeepSeek-V4.1 Flash has 40 transformer layers, a sliding-window size of 128, and shared compressed-KV source layers at 2, 8, 14, and 20. With the current decoder bounded-replay optimization, Prefill still loads the full model: ```text L0-L20: process the full uncached prompt L21-L39: process only the final 128 tokens ``` This saves arithmetic in the late layers, but it has two limitations: 1. Prefill still stores all late decoder weights, even though those layers process only a short window. 2. Prefill usually has few concurrent requests, so the late-layer MoE kernels see only a small number of tokens. The proposed design moves the entire final prompt window to Decode instead of changing the token set in the middle of the model. All Decode layers therefore process the same rows in every step. ## Proposed Design ### Model placement and token split ```mermaid flowchart LR I[Prompt: N tokens] I -->| Compute N-W| P I -->| Compute final W tokens| D subgraph P[Prefill worker: partial model] PE[Encoder L0-L19] PK[L20 KV / Indexer
projection path] PE --> PK end subgraph D[Decode worker: full model] BR[First step: bounded prefill
L0-L39, q_len = W] FT[Sample first token] ND[Later steps: normal decode
L0-L39, q_len = 1 + num_spec_tokens] BR --> FT --> ND end P -->| Transfer N-W KV | D ``` For prompts shorter than the window, P performs no model forward and D processes the complete prompt. For the current checkpoint, the conceptual ownership is: | Worker | Resident model components | Work | | --- | --- | --- | | Prefill | Embedding, causal encoder L0-L19, minimal L20 KV/Indexer projection modules | Prefix `[0, N-W)` | | Decode | Full L0-L39 model and LM head | Final prompt window, first token, and subsequent decode | ### Request flow ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant P as Prefill worker participant D as Decode worker P->>P:

issues.title: Retracted input_embeds requests silently splice two generations into one successful response (send_token_offset survives the discard of output_ids)
issues.body:
# Retracted input_embeds requests silently splice two generations into one successful response (send_token_offset survives the discard of output_ids)

## Summary

When the KV cache pool runs out of memory, the scheduler retracts running decode requests and requeues them. For requests that supplied `input_embeds`, `Req.reset_for_retract()` deliberately discards `output_ids` and restarts generation from scratch (the fix for the shape-mismatch crash in #14109, PR #14110), but it does not reset `send_token_offset` (nor the sibling output-stream cursors). The output streamer slices the restarted generation with that surviving offset, so the first N tokens of the new generation are silently dropped and the client's assembled response becomes a splice of generation A's already-streamed prefix and generation B's tail. The request then finishes normally with a success finish reason.

Affected code (at commit b510881157b8f12b98387340c7fbfc266dbbb35e):

- `python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py:1928-1932`, the input_embeds branch of `reset_for_retract`:

  ```python
  if self.input_embeds is not None:
      self.output_ids = array("q")
      self.weight_version_events = truncate_weight_version_events(
          self.weight_version_events, num_kept_tokens=self.send_token_offset
      )
  ```

  `output_ids` is cleared, `weight_version_events` is truncated using `send_token_offset`, but `send_token_offset` itself is never reset. Its only assignments are initialization to 0 at request creation (`schedule_batch.py:1163-1164`, with `send_decode_id_offset`, and `:1167`/`:1170` for the logprob and sampling-mask offsets) and advancement by the streamer.
- `python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_components/output_streamer.py:451-461`:

  ```python
  send_token_offset = req.send_token_offset
  ...
  output_ids_ = req.output_ids_through_stop
  self.output_ids.append(output_ids_[send_token_offset:])
  req.send_token_offset = len(output_ids_)
  ```

  After the restart, `output_ids_` is the new generation's ids, so the delta skips its first `send_token_offset` tokens. Lines 481-482 repeat the same pattern for `send_decode_id_offset` on the detokenizer path, and the incremental detokenizer cursors (`surr_offset`, `read_offset`, feeding `init_incremental_detokenize`, `schedule_batch.py:1638-1656`) likewise survive with values that assume generation continuity.
- Trigger: `python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py:4076-4089` (`not batch.check_decode_mem()` fires `batch.retract_decode()`). Retraction victim selection prefers requests with the fewest generated tokens (`schedule_batch.py:3254-3290`), i.e. requests early in generation, which are exactly the ones with small nonzero streamed offsets.
- Reachability: `input_embeds` is a client-supplied field of the native generate API (`python/sglang/srt/managers/io_struct.py`, "one can specify either text or input_ids or input_embeds").

#14109 fixed the crash but left the client-visible stream state stale; this report is the residual defect introduced by that fix, not a reopen of the crash.

## Reproduction (engine state machine, no GPU needed)

Executing the verbatim-extracted `reset_for_retract`, `_refresh_fill_ids`, `get_fill_ids` and the real `truncate_weight_version_events` on a request with `input_embeds` set, 64 prompt tokens, 40 streamed output tokens:

1. Before retraction the client has received generation A, tokens 9000..9039; `send_token_offset == 40`.
2. `reset_for_retract()` runs: `output_ids == []`, `

issues.title: [Bug] FP8 KV cache scales are silently dropped when loading Qwen3-MoE / Qwen2 / Mixtral and every layer falls back to scale 1.0
issues.body:
## Describe the bug

When a checkpoint carries FP8 KV cache scales as tensors, the hand-written weight loaders of `Qwen3MoeForCausalLM`, `Qwen2ForCausalLM`, and `MixtralForCausalLM` drop them. `process_weights_after_loading` then sees both scales still at their initial -1.0 and resets them to 1.0.

```python
# python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/kv_cache.py, current main
elif layer.k_scale <= 0.0 and layer.v_scale <= 0.0:
    # If no scales were loaded (both scales are invalid non-positive
    # values), use the default value of 1.0
    k_scale = 1.0
    v_scale = 1.0
```

Every attention layer therefore dequantizes its FP8 cache with a unit scale, and the per-layer error equals the calibrated scale. Outputs stay finite, nothing is raised, and the error is invisible to tensor-level checks.

Three scale namings are affected. llm-compressor stores the scales under the fused projection name, for example `model.layers.0.self_attn.qkv_proj.k_scale` (the layout reported in vllm-project/vllm#25047). ModelOpt stores them per projection, for example `model.layers.0.self_attn.k_proj.k_scale`. The deprecated single `.kv_scale` tensor is lost as well, while the model registers the scales at `self_attn.attn.k_scale` and `self_attn.attn.v_scale`.

### Mechanism

The loaders run their `stacked_params_mapping` loop before the params lookup, and the mapping is a substring replace.

```python
# python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_moe.py, current main
for param_name, weight_name, shard_id in stacked_params_mapping:   # 1186
    if weight_name not in name:
        continue
    ...
    name = name.replace(weight_name, param_name)                   # 1198
    ...
    if name not in params_dict:                                    # 1202
        continue
```

`"v_proj"` is a substring of `"qkv_proj"`, so the fused scale name becomes the nonexistent `self_attn.qkqkv_proj.k_scale`. The per-projection name is rewritten into `self_attn.qkv_proj.k_scale`, which does not exist either because the model keeps the scales on `self_attn.attn`.

| model file                                       | fused naming                       | per-projection naming            | deprecated `.kv_scale` |
| ------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------- | -------------------------------- | ---------------------- |
| `qwen3_moe.py`                                   | dropped, 0 warnings                | dropped, 0 warnings              | dropped, 0 warnings    |
| `qwen2.py` (default `_legacy_load_weights` path) | dropped, 2 "not found" warnings    | dropped, 2 warnings              | dropped, 1 warning     |
| `mixtral.py`                                     | `KeyError` on `qkqkv_proj.k_scale` | `KeyError` on `qkv_proj.k_scale` | silently skipped       |

The dangerous row is qwen3_moe, whose whole path from loading to the 1.0 fallback prints nothing at all. vllm had the same defect in vllm-project/vllm#25047 and at least logged a startup warning there ("Using KV cache scaling factor 1.0 ..."), which is how that issue was noticed. The per-projection layout is the fully silent real-world path, because its `k_proj.weight` / `v_proj.weight` tensors load correctly through the same stacked mapping and the loss touches only the scale tensors.

### Scope and fix shape

sglang already has the bridge for this naming gap. `maybe_remap_kv_scale_name` in `python/sglang/srt/model_loader/weight_utils.py` remaps ModelOpt and deprecated names, and 30 model files

issues.title: [Tracking] Pipeline parallelism x speculative decoding (EAGLE/MTP): converge prefill gate PRs, make the path model-agnostic, decide decode design
issues.body:
## Motivation

Pipeline parallelism and speculative decoding are still gated off against each other, but the pieces to lift the gate have been landing and are now in flight from several authors with overlapping scope. This issue tracks the work so the remaining PRs can converge on one design instead of a per-model allowlist.

Concrete use case: PD-disaggregated serving of large hybrid MoE models (Qwen3.5 / Qwen3.8 / DeepSeek / GLM) where the prefill role runs PP (e.g. PP4 for the InferenceMAX AgentX recipe) and the decode role uses MTP. Today the prefill role only starts with `PYTHONOPTIMIZE=1` to skip the assertion, or with one of the model-specific gate PRs below.

## What is already model-agnostic (merged)

Since #35758 the prefill-side runtime does not depend on the model:

- The draft worker is created only on the last PP stage (`EAGLEWorkerV2._hosts_draft`); other stages return proxy tensors so scheduler dispatch stays rank-uniform.
- `scheduler_pp_mixin` carries the draft output (`draft_topk_p`, `draft_topk_index`, `draft_hidden_states`) along the PP ring and rebinds it as `batch.spec_info` on stage 0 so the PD result contains it.

## What is still model-specific today

**1. Last-stage draft embedding (the only hard dependency).** `EagleDraftWorker.init_lm_head` calls `target.get_embed_and_head()`. On the last stage `embed_tokens` is a `PPMissingLayer` for most targets (`deepseek_v2`, `llama`, `glm4_moe`, ...), so `.weight` raises. Two different fixes exist:

- Qwen3.5 (#37471, merged): the draft keeps its own embedding and `qwen3_5_mtp.load_weights` loads it from the target checkpoint; the target returns `embed=None` on non-first stages.
- DeepSeek / GLM (#39378, open): the target materializes `embed_tokens` on the last stage (`pp_stage_needs_embedding`) and the draft borrows it.

Every new model currently has to pick one and re-implement it in its own model file. The allowlists in #39378 / #39602 / #38698 exist only to express "this model did that work".

**2. Extra `spec_info` fields on the ring.** The ring serializes three hard-coded tensors. DSA models need `draft_dsa_topk_indices` (added by hand in #39378); the next model with extra draft state will need another hand-written field.

**3. EAGLE3 / DFLASH aux-hidden capture is silently disabled under PP.** `set_eagle3_layers_to_capture` / `set_dflash_layers_to_capture` return early on non-last ranks, so capture layers that live on earlier stages are never captured. Affects Llama / gpt-oss / Kimi-K2.5 EAGLE3 drafts. This is a correctness gap, not a gate.

**4. Targets without PP at all.** `qwen3_next.py`, `longcat_flash.py`, `hunyuan_v4.py` have no PP support in the target; PP+MTP is moot there until PP lands.

**5. PD KV transfer under PP** for non-standard pools is being fixed per pool: MLA layer offsets in nixl (#39378), hybrid mamba pools (#33584), QSA / PLE pools (#38698). PP is only permitted on the disagg prefill role, so these block the actual use case.

## Status by model family

| Family | Target PP | Draft embedding on last stage | Ring fields | PD KV under PP |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.5 | yes | yes (#37471) | ok | hybrid pool: #33584 |
| DeepSeek V3 / V3.2, GLM-5 | yes | #39378 | DSA: #39378 | MLA: #39378 |
| Qwen3.8 / Qwen4Exp | #38698 | #38698 | ok | QSA/PLE: #38698 |
| Llama / gpt-oss EAGLE3 | yes | missing | ok | ok | 
| Qwen3-Next, LongCat-Flash, Hunyuan-v4 | missing | missing | missing | missing |

## In-flight PRs

Prefill gate (overlapping):
- #39378

issues.title: [Bug] Rust server assigns the same HTTP port to multiple system-DP replicas
issues.body:
## Description

With ordinary system data parallelism and DP Attention disabled, multiple Rust serving replicas can attempt to bind the same HTTP port, preventing startup.

## Example

Observed on a single Linux host with two CUDA GPUs:

```text
SGLANG_RUST_SERVER=1
model_path: Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B
dp_size: 2
tp_size: 1
pp_size: 1
enable_dp_attention: false
port: 30000
```

Each DP replica has an independent TP group. With `tp_size=1`, both replicas have TP rank zero:

| Replica | DP rank | TP rank | Assigned HTTP port |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| First | 0 | 0 | 30000 |
| Second | 1 | 0 | 30000 |

The captured log shows DP1 starting a listener:

```text
[DP1] SGLANG_RUST_SERVER enabled, Rust server listen on 127.0.0.1:30000 (DP rank 0/2)
```

DP0 subsequently fails:

```text
ValueError: runtime start failed: binding API listener on 127.0.0.1:30000 failed: Address already in use (os error 98)
```

The `DP rank 0/2` suffix is also misleading: it uses the attention DP rank, which is zero when DP Attention is disabled.

## Expected behavior

Each Rust listener on the same host should receive a distinct port. For this configuration:

```text
DP0 → 30000
DP1 → 30001
```

Only the designated leader within each replica should start a listener. Other TP workers should continue receiving requests through internal communication.

## Cause

The existing port-offset calculation derives the listener's identity from its position within the TP group. That does not distinguish ordinary system-DP replicas, because each replica has its own TP group starting at rank zero.

Python serving does not encounter this particular collision: it uses a shared HTTP frontend and routes requests internally to the DP schedulers.

This issue concerns ordinary system DP. DP Attention uses a different rank layout and requires its existing node-local listener-port calculation.

Related fix PR: #39932.

issues.title: [Bug] Rust server cannot find a cached tokenizer when the model revision is a commit SHA
issues.body:
## Description

Rust serving can fail to start when a Hugging Face model is specified by its repository ID and a full commit SHA, even though the tokenizer for that revision is already cached locally.

## Example

Observed on Apple Silicon/MLX with these settings:

```text
SGLANG_RUST_SERVER=1
model_path: mlx-community/Qwen3-0.6B-4bit
revision: 73e3e38d981303bc594367cd910ea6eb48349da8
device: mps
```

The cache contains:

```text
models--mlx-community--Qwen3-0.6B-4bit/
└── snapshots/
    └── 73e3e38d981303bc594367cd910ea6eb48349da8/
        └── tokenizer.json
```

There is no corresponding `refs/73e3e38d981303bc594367cd910ea6eb48349da8` file. A commit-pinned snapshot does not require that reference file.

Despite `tokenizer.json` being present, Rust startup fails with:

```text
ValueError: runtime start failed: tokenizer.json not found for 'mlx-community/Qwen3-0.6B-4bit'
```

Python serving successfully loaded the same pinned model. An offline lookup using Python's Hugging Face client also resolved the cached tokenizer without the `refs/<SHA>` file.

## Expected behavior

Rust should resolve the tokenizer directly from the cached snapshot when the requested revision is a full commit SHA.

## Cause

The Rust lookup uses `hf-hub 0.4.3`'s `CacheRepo::get()`, which first reads `refs/<revision>` to obtain a snapshot commit. For a commit SHA supplied directly as the revision, the missing ref causes the lookup to return `None` before checking the existing snapshot.

This is a cache-resolution issue, rather than a missing model file or an MLX inference failure. Providing the local snapshot directory directly bypasses the affected lookup.

Related fix PR: #39932.

issues.title: [Bug] FlashKDA prefill returns a tuple and crashes GLM-5.3-Flash with radix cache disabled

`FlashKDAKernel.extend()` returns `(output, None)` on the fused path even when `return_intermediate_states=False`. `KDABackend.forward_extend()` only unpacks the result when `track_ssm` is true. With tracking disabled, GLM-5.3-Flash passes the tuple to gated RMSNorm and crashes:

--linear-attn-prefill-backend flashkda
--linear-attn-decode-backend flashinfer
--linear-attn-verify-backend triton
--mamba-ssm-dtype bfloat16
--moe-runner-backend deep_gemm
--disable-radix-cache
--speculative-algorithm DFLASH --speculative-dflash-block-size 8
```

With a compatible FlashKDA installation and the model/draft loaded, send:
```python
import requests
requests.post("http://localhost:30000/generate", json={
    "input_ids": [1000] * 128,
    "sampling_params": {"temperature": 0, "max_new_tokens": 16},
}).raise_for_status()
```

The 128-token input deliberately hits the fused path. Long inputs above the current 2048-token routing threshold, short inputs below 64, or intermediate-state tracking can take the Triton fallback and hide the bug.

### Root cause and proposed fix

The tuple wrapper was added in #33561. Return `self._flashkda_extend(...)` directly. Requests needing intermediate states already take the separate fallback, so its contract should remain unchanged.

### Validation of the minimal fix

- Original full-model run reproduced the exact traceback above; the identical request after the patch returned HTTP 200 and 16 output tokens.
- Real GPU kernel replay: patched output and updated SSM state are bitwise equal to the original tuple's tensor and state; gated norm succeeds with finite output.
- Full-model requests with 32, 128, 1024, 2048, and 4096 input tokens, plus a text chat request, all returned HTTP 200 after the patch.
- These are functional regressions, not accuracy or throughput benchmark claims. No PD transport validation was performed.

issues.title: [Bug] /v1/messages never reports cache_creation_input_tokens, so cache writes are billed as plain input
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] 1. I have searched related issues but cannot get the expected help.
- [ ] 2. The bug has not been fixed in the latest version.

### Describe the bug

We serve an agent fleet through the new-api gateway pointed at sglang's Anthropic-compatible `/v1/messages`, and the `usage` object never carries `cache_creation_input_tokens` — the cache-write event is invisible, so every prefix written to the radix cache on a miss is billed as plain input. Reproduction is Anthropic-shaped on purpose: a long `system` block tagged with an official `cache_control: {"type":"ephemeral"}` breakpoint, issued twice with a fresh prefix. The cold (writing) call returns only `{"input_tokens": 7237, "output_tokens": 6}` — no write field at all — while the warm call on the same prefix returns `{"input_tokens": 901, "output_tokens": 6, "cache_read_input_tokens": 6336}`, and the read accounting itself is exact (901 + 6336 = 7237, fields cleanly mutually exclusive). Per the official API, that first call should instead report the written span through `cache_creation_input_tokens`, which is the field gateways and SDK cost trackers key cache-write pricing on (1.25x / 2x base for 5m / 1h ephemeral TTLs); today that price tier can never engage for sglang traffic. Expected behavior: when a request carries an explicit `cache_control` breakpoint, report the non-hit portion of the cached prefix through `cache_creation_input_tokens` on the writing call.

```bash
# run twice with the same $FRESH_LONG_TEXT (~7k tokens); observe .usage
curl -s $SGLANG/v1/messages -H 'content-type: application/json' -d "{
  \"model\": \"$MODEL\",
  \"system\": [{\"type\":\"text\",\"text\":\"$FRESH_LONG_TEXT\",\"cache_control\":{\"type\":\"ephemeral\"}}],
  \"messages\": [{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"hi\"}], \"max_tokens\": 6
}" | jq .usage
```

### Reproduction

deterministic — see snippet above

### Environment

sglang self-built Docker image, base commit `4ccff141d` (an unrelated internal attention patch; the protocol-layer usage mapping is unmodified)

issues.title: [Bug] Anthropic endpoint: tool_reference parts in tool_result break chat templates without deferred-reference support (HTTP 500)
issues.body:
## Describe the bug

The Anthropic-compatible endpoint (`/v1/messages`) converts `tool_reference` blocks found inside `tool_result` content into structured parts `{"type": "tool_reference", "name": ...}` (deferred tool loading, #22702). That part type is only understood by chat templates that implement deferred-reference expansion (GLM family). For any other model, the template hits the unknown item type and the whole request fails with HTTP 500:

```
jinja2.exceptions.TemplateError: Unexpected item type in content.
... [ts] Anthropic error response api_error (exception=ValueError): Internal server error
```

With Claude Code this is especially disruptive: once a session uses deferred tool loading (ToolSearch) and a `tool_reference` block enters the conversation history, **every subsequent request in that session fails** — the history carries the block forward, so retries cannot recover and only clearing/compacting the context fixes it. We observed ~26 consecutive 500s on a single session until it was abandoned.

## Reproduction

Server: SGLang 0.5.17 (same code on `main`), any model whose chat template does not handle `tool_reference` (reproduced with the stock Qwen3.8-27B template):

```bash
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1/messages \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' -H 'x-api-key: dummy' -d '{
    "model": "qwen3.8-27b",
    "max_tokens": 16,
    "stream": false,
    "tools": [{"name": "DemoTool", "description": "demo", "input_schema": {"type": "object", "properties": {}}}],
    "messages": [
      {"role": "user", "content": "list the deferred tools"},
      {"role": "assistant", "content": [
        {"type": "tool_use", "id": "toolu_1", "name": "ToolSearch", "input": {"query": "select:Foo"}}
      ]},
      {"role": "user", "content": [
        {"type": "tool_result", "tool_use_id": "toolu_1", "content": [
          {"type": "text", "text": "Found 1 tool:"},
          {"type": "tool_reference", "tool_name": "DemoTool"}
        ]}
      ]},
      {"role": "user", "content": "now use it"}
    ]
  }'
```

Actual: `HTTP 500 {"type":"error","error":{"type":"api_error","message":"Internal server error"}}` with `TemplateError: Unexpected item type in content` in the server log.
Same request with the `tool_reference` item removed: `HTTP 200`. (A `thinking` block in assistant history does not trigger this; the minimal trigger is the `tool_reference` item in a `tool_result` content list.)

## Root cause

`python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/anthropic/serving.py`, `_convert_to_chat_completion_request` → `_convert_tool_result_content`:

```python
elif item_type == "tool_reference":
    ref_name = item.get("tool_name") or item.get("name")
    if ref_name:
        tool_content_parts.append(
            {"type": "tool_reference", "name": ref_name}
        )
```

The structured part is emitted unconditionally. Templates without deferred-reference expansion (e.g. Qwen's `render_content` macro, which only accepts `text`/`image`/`video` items) raise `TemplateError`, which is surfaced as a 500.

Suggested fix: detect whether the loaded chat template handles `tool_reference` (e.g. substring check on the template source, mirroring how the unit tests fake `tokenizer_manager.tokenizer.chat_template`) and, when it does not, degrade the reference to a text part such as `[tool reference: <name>]` so history echoes keep working for all models while GLM behavior is preserved. A PR implementing this is coming.

issues.title: [Bug] GLM-5.x NoPE MLA (qk_rope_head_dim=0) cannot run on SM120: every DSA sparse-MLA backend is unavailable
issues.body:
## Summary

GLM-5.x uses **NoPE MLA**: `qk_rope_head_dim = 0`, so the absorbed query head dim is
`kv_lora_rank` (512) rather than the DeepSeek `512 + 64 = 576`.

On **SM120** (RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, compute capability 12.0) this model cannot be served at
all. Every `--dsa-prefill-backend` / `--dsa-decode-backend` choice fails, each for a distinct
reason, and the one backend the code *forces* for GLM + fp8 KV + SM120 is the one whose
FlashInfer kernel rejects NoPE. So with `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3` the model is unrunnable by
construction; with bf16 KV the remaining backends are each blocked as documented below.

This is not specific to any quantized/pruned repack — the geometry below comes from the model
config and applies to the full model too.

## Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| GPU | NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Workstation Edition, SM120 (cc 12.0), 96 GB |
| Driver | 596.72 |
| OS | Windows 11 + WSL2 Ubuntu 24.04 |
| torch | 2.13.0+cu130 (CUDA 13.0) |
| sglang | 0.5.19 |
| flashinfer | 0.6.18 |
| tilelang | 0.1.12 |
| nvcc | 13.4.59 |

Model (same geometry as the official GLM-5.3-Flash; observed on
`Asilarkness/GLM-5.3-Flash-Uncensored-NVFP4-Pruning-62GB`, a fingerprint-preserving repack):

```json
"architectures": ["Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration"],
"num_attention_heads": 64, "kv_lora_rank": 512,
"qk_nope_head_dim": 256, "qk_rope_head_dim": 0, "v_head_dim": 256,
"mla_use_nope": true, "index_topk": 2048
```

Note this matches flashinfer's own `nope_mla_dimensions` preset
(`qk_nope_head_dim=256, qk_rope_head_dim=0, v_head_dim=256, kv_lora_rank=512`) exactly, so NoPE
MLA is a first-class geometry upstream — just not on SM120.

## Device constraint (verified)

`cudaDevAttrMaxSharedMemoryPerBlockOptin` on this part is **101376 B (99 KB)**
(`sharedMemPerMultiprocessor` = 102400). Verified with a minimal CUDA program:
`cudaFuncSetAttribute(k, cudaFuncAttributeMaxDynamicSharedMemorySize, n)` returns
`invalid argument` for n ∈ {131072, 163840, 202752, 206848} and succeeds at 101376.
Hopper/B200 expose ~228 KB, which is the budget the kernels below are written against.

## Failure 1 — `--dsa-prefill-backend tilelang` (bf16 KV): needs 202 KB, device allows 99 KB

```
--dsa-prefill-backend tilelang --dsa-decode-backend tilelang --kv-cache-dtype bfloat16
```

```
File ".../sglang/kernels/ops/attention/dsa/tilelang_kernel.py", line 1397, in tilelang_sparse_fwd
    out = kernel(q.unsqueeze(0), kv.unsqueeze(0), indices.unsqueeze(0))
  ...
tvm.error.InternalError: Failed to set the allowed dynamic shared memory size to 206848
```

`tail_dim == 0` for NoPE, so this routes to `sparse_attention_fwd_kernel_v1`. Its shared
footprint with `num_heads=64, dim=512, block_I=64, bf16` is:

```
Q_shared     [64, 512] * 2 = 65536
KV_shared    [64, 512] * 2 = 65536
O_shared     [64, 512] * 2 = 65536
S_shared     [64,  64] * 2 =  8192
                             ------
                             204800   (+ padding -> the reported 206848)
```

Two observations:

1. **`O_shared` is dead.** It is written by `T.copy(acc_o, O_shared)` and never read — the very
   next line copies `acc_o` straight to `Output`. That is 64 KB allocated for nothing, and on
   SM120 it is fatal on its own (Q + O = 128 KB already exceeds the 99 KB opt-in ceiling).
2. Even without it, the default tile does not fit. The only remaining lever is the KV tile:
   `block_I=16` brings it to ~84 KB, but at that t

issues.body:

### Describe the bug

`python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/encoding_dsv41.py` (added in #39665) carries the pre-release reasoning-effort budget table, `low`/`high`/`xhigh` → 25/50/75. DeepSeek replaced that table on release day, so the prefix SGLang renders at index 0 of every thinking-mode V4.1 prompt no longer matches the model's own reference encoder or `deepseek-recipe`:

| source | low | high | xhigh | max |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash` `encoding/encoding.py`, pre-release revision `fb2764a5` | 25 | 50 | 75 | 100 |
| same file from revision `df42c109` (2026-09-10) onward, current `dba1be0a` | 50 | 75 | — | 100 |
| `deepseek-recipe`, `deepseek-recipe-encoding/src/v4/dsv41.rs` (`reasoning_effort_template`) | 50 | 75 | 75 | 100 |
| SGLang main (`REASONING_EFFORT_MAPPINGS`, `encoding_dsv41.py` L68-73) | 25 | 50 | 75 | 100 |

Effect: a request with `reasoning_effort="high"`, or one that only switches thinking on and takes the server default (`high`), renders `Reasoning Effort: 50 (range 1-100, ...)` on SGLang while DeepSeek's reference and recipe render `Reasoning Effort: 75`; `low` renders 25 instead of 50. `max` is 100 in both tables, so evaluations run at `max` are unaffected. The model repository's `encoding/README.md` states the release mapping explicitly: `"low"` → 50, `"high"` → 75, `"max"` → 100, default `"high"`.

Apart from that line the SGLang encoder and the reference file agree byte-for-byte on the five cases under the model's `encoding/tests/` and on multi-turn, mid-conversation system, kept-reasoning and namespaced-tool conversations (checked with both modules side by side).

Expected: the table should follow the release reference (`low=50, high=75, max=100`); `xhigh` can stay as an alias of `high`, which is what `deepseek-recipe` renders for it. The cookbook sentence listing the tiers (`docs/cookbook/autoregressive/DeepSeek/DeepSeek-V4_1.mdx`) would want the budgets stated as well.

### Reproduction

```python
# ref = encoding/encoding.py downloaded from deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash at revision dba1be0a
from sglang.srt.entrypoints.openai import encoding_dsv41

messages = [
    {"role": "system", "content": "You are a helpful assistant."},
    {"role": "user", "content": "What is 2+2?"},
]
print(ref.encode_messages(messages, thinking_mode="thinking", reasoning_effort="high")[:80])
# <｜begin▁of▁sentence｜><｜System｜>Reasoning Effort: 75 (range 1-100, the higher the value,
print(encoding_dsv41.encode_messages(messages, thinking_mode="thinking", reasoning_effort="high")[:80])
# <｜begin▁of▁sentence｜><｜System｜>Reasoning Effort: 50 (range 1-100, the higher the value,
```

Same result through the server: `reasoning_effort="high"` (or thinking on with no effort set) on `/v1/chat/completions` against `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash` produces the 50 prefix.

### Environment

SGLang main at 923e4a56 (2026-09-17), Python 3.11, Linux x86_64; the rendering is pure string code and does not depend on GPU or kernels. Model: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash`

issues.title: [Bug] /v1/messages streaming thinking blocks can end without a signature
issues.body:
# [Bug] /v1/messages streaming thinking blocks can end without a signature

### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no exact report.
- [x] The bug is present in current `main`.
- [x] This report includes environment information and a minimal reproducer.
- [x] This report is in English.

### Describe the bug

For an open-weight reasoning backend that does not produce an Anthropic cryptographic thinking signature, SGLang's `/v1/messages` adapter emits a streaming thinking block without any `signature` across the complete block lifecycle.

The stream starts with:

```json
{"type":"content_block_start","index":0,"content_block":{"type":"thinking","thinking":""}}
```

It emits `thinking_delta` events, then closes the block without a `signature_delta`.

In the current implementation, `captured_thinking_signature` is initialized, conditionally emitted, and reset, but it is never assigned. Therefore the comment that streaming already handles signatures is not true for unsigned OpenAI-compatible backends such as Qwen.

This can crash the official Anthropic Python SDK during cold concurrent stream initialization. With `anthropic==0.87.0` and `pydantic==2.13.4`, the nested `content_block` can remain a raw dictionary. The SDK accumulator then fails at:

```text
anthropic/lib/streaming/_messages.py:461
AttributeError: 'dict' object has no attribute 'model_dump'
```

The production trigger was two first requests in a fresh process starting together: the main agent turn and an automatic title-generation request. Retrying in the same process continued to fail after the parser cache was initialized incorrectly. Serial replay did not reproduce because the first request warmed the type adapter before the next request.

### Affected code

Current `main`:

```python
if delta.reasoning_content:
    for event in _ensure_content_block_events(
        "thinking",
        ThinkingBlock(thinking=""),
    ):
        yield _emit(event)
```

The non-streaming path also constructs `ThinkingBlock` without a fallback signature.

### Minimal parser reproducer

Run this in a fresh Python interpreter:

```python
from collections import Counter
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
from threading import Barrier

from anthropic._models import construct_type
from anthropic.types import RawMessageStreamEvent

workers = 64
barrier = Barrier(workers)
event = {
    "type": "content_block_start",
    "index": 0,
    "content_block": {"type": "thinking", "thinking": ""},
}


def parse_once(_):
    barrier.wait()
    value = construct_type(value=event, type_=RawMessageStreamEvent)
    return type(value.content_block).__name__


with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=workers) as pool:
    print(Counter(pool.map(parse_once, range(workers))))
```

Observed across representative cold runs:

```text
Counter({'dict': 62, 'ThinkingBlock': 2})
Counter({'dict': 63, 'ThinkingBlock': 1})
```

Adding a non-empty signature to the start block produced:

```text
Counter({'ThinkingBlock': 64})
```

### Expected behavior

For backends that do not provide a native Anthropic thinking signature, SGLang should emit a stable compatibility signature so the completed thinking block is valid and strict SDKs consistently hydrate it as `ThinkingBlock`.

### Proposed fix

Use the same fallback already proposed for the non-streaming path in #29242:

```python
ThinkingBlock(thinking="", signature="sglang")
```

Apply it to both streaming and non-streaming response construction, and ass

issues.title: [RFC] Pluggable KV Compression for Disaggregated Serving
issues.body: ### Checklist - [x] If this is not a feature request but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Motivation ## Summary This RFC proposes an optional KV compression path for Prefill-to-Decode transfer over Mooncake RDMA. SGLang would manage layout preparation, bounded buffers, transfer metadata, and asynchronous completion through a small internal interface for compression backends. Attention would continue to read the existing GPU KV format after received data has been restored. The initial implementation targets lossless P/D transfer on one explicitly supported MHA/GQA layout. The architecture also includes a path toward reusing compressed payloads and integrating with HiCache, with those capabilities delivered as separate extensions. This is a design proposal. No compression ratio or serving speedup has been established. The immediate review request concerns the integration boundary and validation plan; broader support would depend on correctness and measurable benefit. ## Motivation and Scope In P/D serving, KV transfer can delay the handoff from Prefill to Decode. Compression can reduce the transferred bytes, but adds computation, memory traffic, synchronization, and temporary storage. Whether it helps depends on the actual KV distribution, effective network bandwidth, and concurrent model execution. The appropriate algorithm can change with the workload and hardware. Integrating each algorithm directly into the transfer path would repeat page extraction, buffer management, length publication, restoration, and failure handling. A small shared interface would allow these mechanisms to remain in SGLang while the data transformation can be replaced and evaluated independently. Its value must be demonstrated through a real backend rather than assumed from generality alone. For scale, [[Qwen3-8B’s configuration](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-8B/raw/main/config.json)](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-8B/raw/main/config.json) has 36 layers, eight KV heads, and a head dimension of 128. BF16 K and V therefore occupy 144 KiB per valid token, or 1.125 GiB for 8,192 tokens at TP=1, excluding padding and metadata. If the transferred bytes were reduced by 20%, the ideal network saving would be approximately 9.66 ms at 200 Gb/s or 4.83 ms at 400 Gb/s. These are illustrative calculations, not measurements or predictions of compressibility; the additional critical-path cost must fit within the actual saving. The first validation target is Qwen3-8B with BF16 KV, one Prefill worker and one Decode worker, TP/PP/CP/DCP set to one, and GPU LZ4 through nvCOMP. The experiment would pin the attention backend, KV pool layout, page size, dependency versions, and block-size policy. CPU execution, topology conversion, MLA, hybrid state, speculative decoding, HiSparse, and compressed storage are subsequent validation scopes. P/D compression does not require HiCache or persistent offloading. It does not reduce the KV capacity or per-step KV reads required by active attention. GPU compression preserves attention’s input format but still competes for compute and memory bandwidth. ## Proposed Design ### Overall Architecture *Figure 1. The complete proposed architectur

issues.body:
## Checklist

- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

## Motivation

MoonshotAI publishes [Kimi-Vendor-Verifier](https://github.com/MoonshotAI/Kimi-Vendor-Verifier) (KVV), the conformance suite a Kimi-K3 serving endpoint is expected to pass before it is listed as a vendor. It drives a live OpenAI-compatible endpoint and checks three things:

1. **Tool-schema suite**: tool definitions the reference service accepts (non-ASCII property names, draft-07 `$id`, dynamic tools declared in a content-less system message, `tool_choice=required` in various combinations) must produce a tool call.
2. **Stream-spec suite** (22 cases): the exact SSE frame shape of `/v1/chat/completions` with `stream=true`, including Moonshot's extensions (`thinking` request object, `X-Msh-Usage-*` headers, `stream_options.include_internal_content`, per-choice usage on the end frame, reasoning end-of-thinking boundary frame).
3. **BEAM**: a 1M-context multi-turn accuracy run, LLM-judged.

Running KVV against sglang serving `moonshotai/Kimi-K3` on main showed the request and wire-shape layers were the gap, not the model forward: 8 of the 22 stream-spec cases failed on a single cause (`reasoning_content: null` on every frame), most of the remaining ones on tool-call chunk shape, id format and missing extensions, and the tool-schema suite failed mostly because a forced tool call with reasoning off ran to `max_tokens` without ever emitting a call. BEAM surfaced the skipped-think empty-content problem that #34187 already fixed on main.

This issue tracks the remaining PRs so reviewers see the dependency in one place. All changes are gated on the `kimi_k3` chat encoding / tool-call parser and do not move any other model's wire shape.

## PRs

| Suite | PR | Scope |
|---|---|---|
| BEAM | #34187 (merged) | opt-in `force_nonempty_content`: skipped-think answers no longer come back as empty `content` |

issues.title: [Roadmap][Feature] Support T-Head PPU
issues.body:
# [Roadmap][Feature] Support T-Head PPU ## 1. Motivation & Background This roadmap describes upstreaming **first-class support for T-Head PPU** (ZW810 / ZW810E, and the ZW-M890P card) into SGLang. ZW810, ZW810E, and ZW-M890P are hereafter abbreviated to 810, 810e, and 890p, respectively. T-Head PPU exposes a **CUDA-compatible API** through its torch backend (`torch.device("cuda")` is the only valid device type for PPU in PyTorch), so SGLang can run on PPU with a **vendor-isolated branching model**: we keep upstream CUDA code paths untouched wherever possible, detect the platform at runtime, and inject PPU-optimized implementations only where they matter. The work has already been validated internally across a broad model matrix (DeepSeek-R1/V3.2/V4, GLM-4.5/5.2, Kimi-K2.5/K2.6/K3, Qwen3 / Qwen3.5-397B-A17B, MiniMax-M2.7/M3, MiMo-V2.5-Pro, Llama4) with quantizations **bf16 / fp8 / mxfp4 / w8a8-int8 / w4a8-int8 / awq / gptq-marlin**, and features **TP / EP (DeepEP) / DP-attention / PD-disaggregation / EAGLE(E3) & MTP speculative decoding / CUDA graph (incl. piecewise) / context parallelism (incl. cross-machine) / DSA sparse prefill**. ## 2. High-Level Approach ### 2.1 Core strategies Four core strategies: 1. **Progressive PPU branching** — introduce a `PlatformEnum.PPU` / `PPUSRTPlatform` that inherits CUDA behavior, detected via the `PPU_SDK` environment variable. `is_cuda()` stays `True` and `device_type` stays `"cuda"` for PyTorch compatibility, so PPU changes are additive and cannot regress CUDA users. 2. **Plugin-hook injection instead of code edits** — use the existing `sglang.srt.plugins.hook_registry` (`@plugin_hook` with `HookType.REPLACE` / `AROUND`) to swap PPU attention ops (FA3, FlashMLA, DSA) into the community backends **without modifying `flashattention_backend.py` / `flashmla_backend.py` themselves**. Hooks are loaded from `platforms/ppu.py` only when `PPU_SDK` is present. 3. **Build-time adaptation** — AOT `sgl-kernel` build via `setup_ppu.py` / `pyproject_ppu.toml` / `common_extension_ppu.cc` targeting PPU 810/810e/890p (810/810e are roughly SM80-equivalent; 890p is roughly SM89-equivalent), plus a new `get_jit_cuda_arch_suffix()` interface so 810/810e devices JIT-compile with the `sm80a` arch variant. 4. **Targeted optimizations & tuned configs** — PPU-specific kernels (fused silu+mul+quant, DSA/DSv4 indexer quantization & topk kernels, INT8 indexer cache, FLA fast path) and shipped Triton/DeepGEMM tuned configs for `PPU-ZW810`, `PPU-ZW810E`, `ZW-M890P`, all gated behind `SGLANG_PPU_*` env flags with automatic fallback to the community paths. ### 2.2 Three-layer library mapping SGLang sits on the upper layers — the model layer on top, the backend layer in the middle — while the bottom layer is the PPU ops provided by the T-Head SAIL software libraries, injected into the backends via plugin hooks and env-flag dispatch: ```mermaid flowchart TB subgraph SG_MODELS["Model layer (SGLang)"] MODELS["models: DeepSeek / GLM / Kimi / Qwen / ..."] end subgraph SG_BACKENDS["Backend layer (SGLang)"] ATT["attention backends
fa3 / flashmla / dsa / dsv4"] MOE["MoE runner

issues.title: HellaSwag accuracy test cannot run: rowanz/hellaswag is blocked (HTTP 451), breaking base-a and stage-a-amd on every PR
issues.body:
### Summary

`test_hellaswag_select` downloads the HellaSwag validation set from the `rowanz/hellaswag` GitHub repo. That repo is now blocked, so the download can never succeed and every CI run that reaches `test_basic_sanity.py` fails on the download rather than on the change under test.

### The URL is gone for good

```
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rowanz/hellaswag/master/data/hellaswag_val.jsonl   -> 404
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rowanz/hellaswag/main/data/hellaswag_val.jsonl     -> 404
https://github.com/rowanz/hellaswag/raw/master/data/hellaswag_val.jsonl              -> 451
https://api.github.com/repos/rowanz/hellaswag                                        -> 451  {"message": "Repository access blocked"}
```

HTTP 451 on the repo itself means this is not a moved file or a renamed default branch — the whole repository is unavailable, so no path or branch fix brings it back.

The URL is at `python/sglang/test/test_programs.py:519`:

```python
url = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rowanz/hellaswag/master/data/hellaswag_val.jsonl"
filename = download_and_cache_file(url)
lines = list(read_jsonl(filename))
```

### What it breaks

`download_and_cache_file` calls `raise_for_status()`, `retry()` exhausts, and the test errors out:

```
File "/sglang-checkout/python/sglang/test/kits/hellaswag_kit.py", line 22, in test_accuracy_floor
    accuracy, _ = test_hellaswag_select()
File "/sglang-checkout/python/sglang/test/test_programs.py", line 520, in test_hellaswag_select
    filename = download_and_cache_file(url)
requests.exceptions.HTTPError: 404 Client Error: Not Found for url: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rowanz/hellaswag/master/data/hellaswag_val.jsonl
Exception: retry() exceed maximum number of retries.
✗ FAILED: /sglang-checkout/test/registered/core/test_basic_sanity.py returned exit code 1
```

`test_basic_sanity.py` mixes in `HellaswagMixin` and is registered for both suites:

```python
register_cuda_ci(est_time=97, stage="base-a", runner_config="1-gpu-small")
register_amd_ci(est_time=160, suite="stage-a-test-1-gpu-small-amd")
```

so this is not AMD-specific. It reproduces on unrelated branches — `add_aiter_allreduce_fusion` and `fix/pd-kv-checksum-followups` both fail the AMD job with the identical traceback. Because the failure looks like a test failure on the PR, it costs every contributor a round of triage to establish it is not theirs.

### Proposed fix

Read the validation split from `Rowan/hellaswag` on the Hub, which is the dataset's canonical mirror, public and ungated, and carries the same 10042 rows with the fields this test uses. `datasets` is already a declared dependency and `load_dataset` is already how `simple_eval_mmmu_vlm.py` and `kl_test_utils.py` pull their data, so nothing new is introduced.

One difference matters: the Hub copy types `label` as a string where the jsonl had an int. `label` indexes `endings` when building the few-shot examples, and `labels` is compared against the integer `preds` through numpy — a string column would silently make every comparison false and report 0.000 accuracy against a 0.60 floor. It needs coercing on the way in.

Verified against the mirror: 10042 rows, `activity_label` / `ctx` / `endings` / `label` all present, four endings per question, few-shot prompts render identically, and scoring the known labels back through the accuracy expression returns 1.000.

PR to follow.

issues.title: [Bug] OpenAI Chat Completions: Python SSE chunks have inconsistent id and created
issues.body:
Python’s `POST /v1/chat/completions` with `stream=true` exhibits two inconsistencies:

- **`id`:** With `n > 1`, the top-level ID changes between candidates within the same stream.
- **`created`:** When generation crosses a second boundary, the timestamp can change between chunks. This also occurs with `n=1`.

Illustrative example:

| Chunk | `choices[].index` | `id` | `created` |
|---|---:|---|---:|
| 1 | 0 | A | 100 |
| 2 | 1 | B | 100 |
| 3 | 0 | A | 101 |

**Expected:** Every chunk in one Chat Completion should share the same `id` and `created`; candidates are distinguished by `choices[].index`. This is specified in the [OpenAI streaming reference](https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/chat/subresources/completions/streaming-events#chat.completion.chunk).

Both issues were observed on **CUDA and MLX**. Rust maintained consistent values in the corresponding tested streams.

issues.title: [Bug] Potential DSpark startup hang from an unsynchronized CUDA graph memory check
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

DSpark explicitly supports DP attention with a DeepSeek-V4/MoE draft when attention TP size is 1 and full TP size is greater than 1 ([configuration check](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/46ae84df159e261fa67d5cce3647f3342fe365a7/python/sglang/srt/speculative/dspark_components/dspark_worker_v2.py#L148-L165)). In this configuration, [`DsparkWorkerV2`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/46ae84df159e261fa67d5cce3647f3342fe365a7/python/sglang/srt/speculative/dspark_components/dspark_worker_v2.py#L213-L223) constructs `SpecTpSync` with the singleton `attn_tp_group`, while the draft CUDA graph uses the larger `tp_group`. The memory query passes the larger group to [`available_memory_gb`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/46ae84df159e261fa67d5cce3647f3342fe365a7/python/sglang/srt/speculative/dspark_components/dspark_worker_v2.py#L433-L443), but [`SpecTpSync.__init__`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/46ae84df159e261fa67d5cce3647f3342fe365a7/python/sglang/srt/speculative/spec_tp_sync.py#L99-L129) has already disabled every sync site because its constructor group has one rank. The memory helper therefore reads rank-local free memory instead of reducing the minimum over the supplied full-TP group.

DSpark disables decode graph capture below 1 GiB. If rank-local readings fall on opposite sides of that threshold, low-memory ranks pass `capture_decode_cuda_graph=False` and [skip decode capture](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/46ae84df159e261fa67d5cce3647f3342fe365a7/python/sglang/srt/model_executor/model_runner_components/cuda_graph_setup.py#L245-L295), while other ranks enter capture. The capture backend uses [`model_runner.tp_group`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/46ae84df159e261fa67d5cce3647f3342fe365a7/python/sglang/srt/model_executor/runner_backend/full_cuda_graph_backend.py#L82-L95), and each of its two warmups executes a [full-group barrier followed by a model forward](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/46ae84df159e261fa67d5cce3647f3342fe365a7/python/sglang/srt/model_executor/runner_backend/full_cuda_graph_backend.py#L137-L145). Ranks that skipped capture do not execute the matching sequence, so initialization can stall or fail. This requires DSpark, DP attention, a DeepSeek-V4/MoE draft, attention TP size 1, full TP size greater than 1, decode graphs enabled, and memory readings on opposite sides of 1 GiB.

### Reproduction

```python
from types import SimpleNamespace
from unittest.mock import patch

from sglang.srt.speculative.spec_tp_sync import SpecTpSync, SpecTpSyncSite

attention_tp1 = SimpleNamespace(world_size=1)
full_tp2 = SimpleNamespace(world_size=2, cpu_group=object())
sync = SpecTpSync(attention_tp1)

with patch(
    "sglang.srt.speculative.spec_tp_sync.get_available_gpu_memory",
    return_value=2.0,
) as get_memory:
    sync.available_memory_gb(SpecTpSyncSite.DSPARK_MEM, "cuda", 0, group=full_tp2)
    print(get_memory.call_args.kwargs["distributed"])
```

Observed output:

```text
False
``

issues.title: [Bug] --ple-offload-embedding is unreachable when the PLE table exceeds single-device VRAM (embedding is materialised on device before being offloaded)
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] 1. I have searched related issues but cannot get the expected help.
- [x] 2. The bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] 3. Please note that if the bug-related issue you submitted lacks corresponding environment info and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be challenging for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, reducing the likelihood of receiving feedback.
- [x] 4. If the issue you raised is not a bug but a question, please raise a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions/new/choose.
- [x] 5. Please use English, otherwise it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

`--ple-offload-embedding` cannot be reached when the per-rank PLE table is larger than a single device's free VRAM — which is the situation the flag exists for.

The n-gram embedding is materialised on the device first and only then wrapped for host storage:

```python
# python/sglang/srt/models/qwen4_exp.py
926:  self.ple_embedding = Qwen4ExpNGramEmbedding(        # allocates on DEVICE
927:      config, self.ple_embed_dim, ple_layer_index=ple_layer_index,
928:      quant_config=quant_config, prefix=...,
929:  )
933:  if config.ple_offload_embedding:
934:      self.ple_embedding.ngram_embedding = Qwen4ExpPinnedHostEmbedding(
935:          self.ple_embedding.ngram_embedding,
936:          backend=getattr(config, "ple_offload_backend", "pinned"),
937:          table_dir=getattr(config, "ple_offload_dir", None),
938:      )
```

`Qwen4ExpPinnedHostEmbedding.__init__` takes an already-constructed `VocabParallelEmbedding` and reads `embedding.weight`, so the device allocation at line 926 has to succeed before the host table at line 822 is ever allocated. On a device that cannot hold the shard, the process OOMs at 926 and line 933 never runs.

On 2× RTX 3090 with `--ple-offload-embedding --ple-offload-backend pinned`, this misses by **1.2%**:

| | |
|---|---|
| PLE table (`ngram_vocab_size_base` 20,000,000 × `ple_embed_dim` 2560, fp8) | 47.68 GiB |
| per rank at TP=2 | **23.84 GiB** |
| usable per RTX 3090 | **23.56 GiB** |
| shortfall | 0.28 GiB |
| host RAM free | 188 GiB (~4× the whole table) |

The requested allocation in the traceback (23.84 GiB) matches the computed per-rank shard exactly, so TP sharding is working; the shard simply has nowhere to land on the way to the host.

Neither escape hatch applies:

- `--ple-offload-backend file` is rejected on this hardware: `--ple-offload-backend file needs a device whose pageable host memory accesses go through the host page tables (unified-memory parts such as GB10). This device reports it does not; use --ple-offload-backend pinned.`
- `--cpu-offload-gb` raises when combined with `--ple-offload-embedding` (`arg_groups/memory_hook.py::handle_offload_compatibility`), so generic layer offload cannot substitute.

A community vLLM fork (`DominikBucko/qwen38-flash-next-2x3090`) stages this table into host RAM on the same 2× RTX 3090 configuration, so the hardware is capable of holding it; the constraint here is the allocation ordering rather than the target.

This looks relevant to the **local device (5090, spark, etc.)** item on the Qwen3.8-Flash-Next roadmap (#38731). A 32 GB card clears the 23.84 GiB shard, but the same ordering will block any configuration whose per-rank table exceeds one device — which is what small-device serving runs into first. It is also adjacent to #36514, though that requests an auxiliary-GPU target rather than the host path.

issues.title: [Bug] OpenAI-compatible API: Python and Rust render different prompts for identical POST /v1/chat/completions requests
issues.body:
### Summary

The Python frontend and `rust/sglang-server` can construct different model inputs from identical `POST /v1/chat/completions` requests.

A real MLX parity run reported **177 prompt tokens in Python versus 167 in Rust** for the same tool-calling request. Offline rendering and tokenization reproduced these counts, confirming an actual input difference rather than a usage-reporting discrepancy.

### Environment

- Commit: `b9b4b36216ba681f507562d5ce47d400294c7b23`
- Backend: MLX, Apple M3 Max
- Model: `Qwen3-0.6B-4bit`
- Model revision: `73e3e38d981303bc594367cd910ea6eb48349da8`
- Tool parser: `qwen25`

### E2E finding: tool defaults enter the prompt differently

The request omitted `function.strict` and outer `tool.defer_loading`.

Python’s `Tool.model_dump()` includes:

```text
function.strict: false
tool.defer_loading: null
```

Rust omits both. The Qwen template serializes the tool definition into prompt text, so these defaults become model-input tokens.

Controlled rendering checks showed that `strict: false` adds **4 tokens** and outer `defer_loading: null` adds **6**, accounting for the 10-token gap.

### Additional offline findings

Using the same Qwen model template and tokenizer, we also reproduced:

| Input or condition | Python | Rust |
|---|---|---|
| Omitted/null `function.description` | Renders `null` | Renders `""` |
| Omitted/null `function.parameters` | Includes `"parameters": null` | Omits the field |
| Parameter object missing `type` or `properties` | Preserves the object | Adds the missing members |
| Named `tool_choice` with multiple tools | Renders only the selected tool | Renders all tools |
| Multiple text content parts | Joins with spaces | Joins with newlines |
| Final assistant message / `continue_final_message` | Applies role or continuation-prefix handling | Preserves the assistant turn and adds another generation header; the flag has no effect |
| `reasoning_effort: "none"` | Sets template thinking flags to `false` | Does not apply the same conversion on the tested Qwen path |

For example, text parts `"Hello"` and `"world"` become `Hello world` in Python and `Hello\nworld` in Rust.

Tool-definition key ordering also differs. Equal token counts would therefore not establish equal token sequences.

These additional checks exercised preprocessing and rendering only—not the complete HTTP validation, grammar, or inference paths.

### Root cause

The frontends reuse independently defined API representations as template inputs:

- Python serializes Pydantic objects and applies SGLang-specific preprocessing.
- Rust delegates to Dynamo’s request types and renderer, with different omission and normalization rules.

These differences become prompt text when the template consumes or serializes the affected fields.

### Impact and expected behavior

The original request returned the same `get_weather({"city":"Paris"})` call on both sides, but it forced the function name and constrained the city. That does not establish that the input differences are harmless for less constrained requests.

The frontends should follow an agreed preprocessing contract, verified by comparing rendered prompts and input token IDs. Please clarify whether Rust should match Python’s current behavior or both implementations should adopt revised normalization rules.

Changing only the reported token count would conceal the underlying input difference.

issues.title: [Bug] GLM-5.3-Flash (glm5_next): image requests render a no-multimodal reminder instead of the image placeholder — model never sees the image
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I ran `python -m sglang.check_env` / am on a recent main build (2026-09-16) and can reproduce.
- [x] Searched existing issues; no issue covers this rendering defect for the GLM-5.3-Flash / glm5_next family.

### Describe the bug

Serving `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash` with `--enable-multimodal` accepts image requests, but the model never receives the image. The model's chat template predates vision support: for an image content part it renders an inline reminder

> `<reminder>You are unable to process this image because you don't have multi-modal input ability. Try different methods.</reminder>`

instead of the image placeholder special token. SGLang's `Glm4vImageProcessor` therefore never sees a placeholder token to expand, produces zero ViT feature tokens, and the model answers as if no image were attached (typically restating the reminder).

Two independent defects stack here:

1. **Chat template / processor mismatch (this issue).** No placeholder in the prompt ⇒ nothing for the processor to expand.
2. **Transformers floor.** `transformers` < 5.17 predates the `glm5_next` processor, so `AutoProcessor` silently falls back to a bare tokenizer and the vision tower never runs either. Worth a requirements floor for this family.

### Reproducer

Template level, no server needed:

```python
from transformers import AutoTokenizer

tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash", trust_remote_code=True)
msgs = [{
    "role": "user",
    "content": [
        {"type": "image", "image": "/tmp/card.png"},
        {"type": "text", "text": "Read the code word printed on this image."},
    ],
}]
prompt = tok.apply_chat_template(msgs, tokenize=False, add_generation_prompt=True)
print(prompt)  # shows the no-multimodal reminder, not a placeholder

from sglang.srt.multimodal.processors.glm4v import Glm4vImageProcessor
print("placeholder in prompt:", Glm4vImageProcessor.IMAGE_TOKEN in prompt)  # False
```

End-to-end: launch with `--enable-multimodal` and POST an `image_url` + "What code word appears in this image?". `prompt_tokens` for the image request is only a couple of tokens above the text-only baseline for the same prompt (no ViT expansion, which for even a small image should add hundreds of tokens), and the reply denies seeing the image. With the placeholder injected, the same request adds exactly the expected ViT feature-token count for the image grid and the model reads the image correctly.

### Observed

- Prompt text contains the no-multimodal reminder instead of `Glm4vImageProcessor.IMAGE_TOKEN`.
- Image request token count ≈ text-only baseline; model says it cannot see the image.

### Expected

Image parts render the image placeholder; the processor expands it into ViT features and the model sees the image.

### Suggested fix

In `Glm4vImageProcessor.process_mm_data_async` (`python/sglang/srt/multimodal/processors/glm4v.py`): when image data is present and the prompt lacks `IMAGE_TOKEN`, substitute the no-multimodal reminder with `IMAGE_TOKEN` (one per image; append if the reminder is absent). This is what we run in production and it fixes the family end-to-end on 8xH200 — happy to send a PR.

### Test-coverage gap

`test/registered/e2e/models/test_glm53_flash_h200.py` and `test_glm53_flash_b200.py` exercise this family text-only (GSM8K accuracy + speculative decoding) with no `--enable-multimodal` and no image requests, so per-commit CI cannot catch vision regressions for this family. A small multimodal e2e (e.g.
